subject: Access controls onboarding — exception & implementation plan
messages:
From: Laura Mitchell <laura@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: access controls & service account exceptions

Hi Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting implementation work this week and have a couple of non-standard items we need help coordinating from your side:

- Our CI/CD runners (hosted by InfraProxy) make outbound calls from a small pool of ephemeral IP ranges; they need to be allowed to reach your management endpoints during provisioning.
- We use an IdP that requires a short-lived SAML assertion flow; I can share metadata but want to ensure we don't break SCIM provisioning for nested groups.
- We plan to create a few service accounts in Redwood for automated data ingestion; we expect those accounts to require scoped, auditable keys and a roll policy.

I've attached a simplified network diagram showing the runner NATs and our internal service account patterns (crestline_network_diagram.pdf).

Can we align on an exception approach (temporary CIDR allowlist, per-service account ACLs, and a mutual action plan)? Ideal outcome: go-live with minimal downtime and documented rollback.

Available for a quick kickoff this afternoon or tomorrow morning — suggested duration 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Laura Mitchell
Head of Platform Integrations
Crestline Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Mitchell <laura@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: access controls & service account exceptions

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the diagram — that helps. Proposed immediate plan and information requests so our implementation team can scope the change: 

1) Kickoff: 30-min sync today at 2:00pm PT or tomorrow at 9:00am PT — please confirm.
2) For SSO/SAML: please share IdP metadata XML and the SAML binding preference (POST vs Redirect). We will validate assertion lifetime and recommended NameID format.
3) For SCIM: share a small sample of your user/group hierarchy and any nested group usage we must preserve during provisioning (group IDs preferred).
4) For IP allowlist: list the CIDRs you require access from and whether they are static or ephemeral; if ephemeral, accept that we will use time-boxed temporary exceptions (7 days by default) and monitor for traffic.
5) Service accounts: list each automation account with intended scope and token rotation cadence. We recommend per-service accounts with least privilege and a documented emergency key revocation flow.

Deliverables we can commit to after kickoff:
- Temporary allowlist applied to management endpoints with expiration and audit log enabled.
- SCIM group mapping doc and a dry-run (no writes) against a staging tenant.
- Service account creation + RBAC template and recommended rotation cadence.

Marissa / Ben — can you lead the technical onboarding once Laura confirms the kickoff time? Ben, flag any platform constraints on temporary CIDR exceptions so we can include them in the mutual action plan.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Onboarding: access controls & service account exceptions

Folks — forwarding Crestline's ask. Short summary in case you're jumping in:
- They need temporary allowlist entries for CI/CD runners (ephemeral IPs ideally time-boxed).
- SAML IdP metadata + SCIM group nesting could break our default mappings; they want a staging dry-run.
- Service accounts that will ingest data need scoped tokens and an agreed rotation policy.

Attached diagram from customer. Monica — please own the mutual action plan and the staging dry-run. Karthik — can you confirm whether we can offer a 7-day temporary CIDR exception with automatic expiry and audit logs? If not, what's the alternative?

Forwarded message follows.

--Ben

Subject: Re: Onboarding: access controls & service account exceptions — mutual action plan

Hi Laura —

Thanks — confirmed kickoff for today at 2:00pm PT (calendar invite sent). Attached is a draft mutual action plan (crestline_mutual_action_plan_v1.docx) with owners and dates. High-level summary below: 

Mutual Action Plan (draft)
- Day 0 (kickoff): Align on SAML metadata and list of service accounts — Owner: Laura (Crestline) — Due: 2026-07-30 EOD
- Day 1: Apply temporary CIDR allowlist to management endpoints (7-day expiry, auto-revoke) — Owner: Karthik (Redwood Eng) — Due: 2026-07-31 11:59pm PT
- Day 2: Run SCIM dry-run (read-only) against staging tenant; validate nested group mapping and user attribute mappings — Owner: Monica (CS) + Laura — Due: 2026-08-01
- Day 3: Create service accounts in staging with scoped roles and configure rotation policy; document emergency revocation steps — Owner: Karthik + Monica — Due: 2026-08-02
- Go-live window: after SCIM mapping validated and service accounts tested; rollback plan included in attachment.

Notes / constraints:
- Temporary CIDR exceptions will be logged and monitored; we will also add a short-lived ACL that requires approval from security for any extension beyond 7 days.
- For SAML, if your IdP insists on a nonstandard NameID, we may need one additional validation cycle.

Next steps for you: please upload IdP metadata and a sample SCIM export to the shared Drive link and reply to this thread so I can attach the finalized MAP to the HubSpot deal.

If anything urgent pops up before the kickoff, ping me directly.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
